title: Workload-Identität: wie sich Aufträge, Hosts und Apps ausweisen
summary: Aufbereitung von IP-D10 aus dem Dossier Integrierte Plattform (AGT-W81) für den Owner. Inhalt: Begriffe in einfachen Worten; heutiger Stand im Code (Bearer-Tokens fuer Hosts mit 30 Tagen, dauerhafte Modell-Logins in jedem Lauf, gespeicherte SSH-, kubeconfig- und Cloud-Zugaenge fuer Deploys, App-Passwoerter ohne eigene Identitaet; kurzlebig bereits GitHub-Installations-Tokens und SSH-Zertifikate der Host-CA; Cloud-Run-Adapter mit Foederation, aber ohne Aussteller); Option A konkret (SPIFFE-IDs, JWT- und X.509-SVIDs, OIDC-Foederation zu AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Kubernetes, Anthropic und OpenAI, SSH-Zertifikate, was Studio betreiben muesste, was sich fuer Lauf, Deploy und App aendert); Option B mit Kosten fuer Rotation und Schutz; Vergleich von vier Alternativen (A1 Studio als Aussteller schrittweise, A2 SPIRE sofort, B gespeicherte Schluessel, C externer Aussteller) mit Ausfall des Ausstellers, Schluesseldiebstahl, Migration und Stufen W1 bis W5. Empfehlung: IP-D10 bei A belassen und als A1 schaerfen, Cloud-Deploy-Ziele zuerst, dann Modell-APIs und SSH-Zertifikate. Entscheidungen WI-D1 bis WI-D7; acht Umsetzungsscheiben WI-1 bis WI-8.

implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Inventory of long-lived credentials with holder, expiry and rotation plan

Source: docs/operations/workload-identitaet/index.html (AGT-3876), decisions WI-D6. Read that Dossier and workbench.json first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/operations/security/overview.md and docs/operations/security/secret-provider.md. Use the Dossier's recommended option for each named decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented.

Stage: W3 (runs in parallel to W1). Dependencies: none.

Entry points: backend/Features/Secrets/ (SecretRecords.cs, SecretProvider.cs), the credential registry and Settings > Credentials inventory (search for TaskServerCredentialRegistryStore and the credentials inventory endpoints), backend/Features/Security/Iam/, task-server/TaskServerPrincipalStore.cs.

## Deliver
Classify every credential the inventory lists as `short-lived` (expires by itself within 24 hours, for example GitHub installation tokens, SSH certificates, future workload identity tokens) or `long-lived` (everything else). For each long-lived credential record and show holder, target, creation date, expiry (or `none`), last use when known and a rotation plan (interval and next due date). Add the long-lived entries the Dossier's current-state table names that the inventory does not yet show (provider logins per host, deploy keys and PAT fallbacks, deploy target credentials stored in the secret provider, external store tokens, bootstrap principals without expiry) as metadata only. Warn the Owner in the operator feed 14 days and 3 days before an expiry or a due rotation. Implement WI-D6 option A: a long-lived credential stays allowed where a target has no federation, but is always marked.

## Out of scope
Federation and the issuer (WI-2 onwards). Automatic rotation at the target.

## Acceptance
- Every inventory entry carries the short-lived or long-lived class; long-lived entries show holder, target, expiry and rotation plan, metadata only.
- A credential without expiry shows `none` and a rotation plan; a test proves no value or token prefix is returned by any route.
- Expiry and due-rotation warnings appear at 14 and 3 days in tests with an injected clock.

## Rules
Reproduce each gap with a failing test before the fix. Tests inject the clock (TestClockGuardTests). Every ProcessStartInfo sets CreateNoWindow = true. No empty catch blocks, no whole-file line-ending rewrites. Build any credential-shaped or token-shaped test value at runtime; never write provider-shaped literals. Do not put real hostnames, account ids or addresses into code, tests, docs or commits; the repository is public. No secret or token value may appear in a log, API response, card, audit entry or result file. UI changes follow frontend/AGENTS.md and docs/quality/design/style-guide-hard-rules.md and need Playwright coverage with light and dark screenshots under results/. Update docs/operations/security/overview.md and the affected setup guide, and append a dated entry to the Implementation section of the Dossier. Report the result SHA in status.md.

implementationTasks.title: WI-2 · Workload identity issuer: JWT-SVIDs bound to lease, approval and host, with discovery, JWKS and key rotation
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Workload identity issuer: JWT-SVIDs bound to lease, approval and host, with discovery, JWKS and key rotation

Source: docs/operations/workload-identitaet/index.html (AGT-3876), decisions WI-D1, WI-D4, WI-D5. Read that Dossier and workbench.json first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/operations/security/overview.md and docs/operations/security/secret-provider.md. Use the Dossier's recommended option for each named decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented.

Stage: W1. Dependencies: none.

Entry points: backend/Features/Secrets/SecretWorkloadBinding.cs (lease, deploy job and host binding to reuse), backend/Features/Secrets/BuiltIn/KeyEncryptionKeySource.cs (key custody pattern), backend/Features/QualityStudio/QualityStudioEndpoints.cs and Ed25519Assertion.cs (existing JWKS pattern), backend/Features/Security/ (runner principals, audit writer), backend/Features/Deploy/ (deploy approval).

## Deliver
Add a workload identity issuer to Studio. It signs JWT-SVIDs (RS256 by default) whose `sub` is a SPIFFE ID in the trust domain of the installation: `spiffe://<td>/run/<project>/<card>/<attempt>` for coding and review attempts, `spiffe://<td>/deploy/<project>/<environment>` for deploy jobs, `spiffe://<td>/host/<host-id>` for hosts; `aud` is required and set per request from an allowlist per target; extra claims `studio_project`, `studio_environment`, `studio_release`, `studio_card`, `studio_run`, `studio_approval`; a unique `jti`. Issue only to an authenticated runner for a live lease of that attempt, to a deploy job with a claimed lease and, for production, a recorded approval, reusing SecretWorkloadBinding; refuse otherwise with a typed reason. Lifetimes per WI-D5 option A (token at most 10 minutes). Serve `/.well-known/openid-configuration` and a JWKS under a configurable issuer URL. Keep the signing key like the secret store key-encryption key (WI-D4 option A: OS key store or an owner-only file outside the workspace) behind an `IWorkloadSigner` interface so a KMS adapter can follow. Rotate keys automatically (default 90 days): publish the next key at least 24 hours before first use and keep the previous key until its last token expired. Write every issuance and refusal to the hash-chained control plane audit (subject, audience, lease or job, expiry, key id; never the token). Derive the trust domain from the configured public host name, otherwise from the installation id.

## Out of scope
Publication outside Studio and target setup (WI-3). Any consumer of the tokens (WI-4 onwards). X.509-SVIDs (WI-7).

## Acceptance
- A live lease yields a token whose sub, aud, exp and claims match the rules; an expired or foreign lease, a deploy without approval for production, and an audience outside the allowlist are refused with typed reasons.
- Tokens verify against the served JWKS with a standard JWT library; a rotated key is served before its first use and the old key stays until expiry, proven with an injected clock.
- The signing key never appears in the workspace, API responses or logs; restart keeps the same key.
- Each issuance and refusal writes one audit entry without the token.

## Rules
Reproduce each gap with a failing test before the fix. Tests inject the clock (TestClockGuardTests). Every ProcessStartInfo sets CreateNoWindow = true. No empty catch blocks, no whole-file line-ending rewrites. Build any credential-shaped or token-shaped test value at runtime; never write provider-shaped literals. Do not put real hostnames, account ids or addresses into code, tests, docs or commits; the repository is public. No secret or token value may appear in a log, API response, card, audit entry or result file. UI changes follow frontend/AGENTS.md and docs/quality/design/style-guide-hard-rules.md and need Playwright coverage with light and dark screenshots under results/. Update docs/operations/security/overview.md and the affected setup guide, and append a dated entry to the Implementation section of the Dossier. Report the result SHA in status.md.

# Federated cloud and Kubernetes deploys without stored target keys

Source: docs/operations/workload-identitaet/index.html (AGT-3876), decisions WI-D1, WI-D6. Read that Dossier and workbench.json first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/operations/security/overview.md and docs/operations/security/secret-provider.md. Use the Dossier's recommended option for each named decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented.

Stage: W1. Dependencies: WI-2, WI-3.

Entry points: runner/DeployAdapters/ (CloudRunDeployAdapter.cs, KubernetesDeployAdapter.cs, DeployTargetContracts.cs), runner/DeployHostCommand.cs (live deploy path), backend/Features/Secrets/SecretWorkloadBinding.cs, the issuer from WI-2.

## Deliver
Give deploy targets a credential mode `federated` next to `stored secret`. In federated mode the deploy job requests a workload identity token for the target's audience from Studio at deploy time and exchanges it at the target: Google Cloud through the existing `external_account` flow of the Cloud Run adapter, now with the Studio-issued token instead of a stored subject token; AWS through `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` with the role from the target settings and a session of at most one hour; Azure through the client assertion flow with the federated identity credential; a self-managed Kubernetes cluster by presenting the token as bearer to an API server that trusts the issuer. The token lives only in the deploy job's temporary directory and is deleted afterwards. Keep stored-secret mode working and mark such targets as long-lived in the inventory (WI-1 when present). If the deploy adapters are still not reachable from the live deploy path, route only targets in federated mode through them and document that in status.md.

## Out of scope
SSH targets (WI-5). Model APIs (WI-6). Automatic creation of cloud roles.

## Acceptance
- With fake STS endpoints for AWS, Google and Azure and a fake Kubernetes API server, a federated deploy succeeds without any stored target secret and fails with a typed reason when the target refuses the token.
- The token and the exchanged credentials never leave the job's temporary directory and are absent from logs and results.
- A production deploy without recorded approval gets no token.

## Rules

# Short-lived SSH certificates for deploys to servers

Source: docs/operations/workload-identitaet/index.html (AGT-3876), decisions WI-D1, WI-D5. ## Deliver
For SSH deploy targets add a credential mode `certificate`. Sign host certificates for enrolled targets so the job verifies the server against the CA instead of a stored known_hosts entry, with known_hosts as fallback. Revocation uses the existing KRL path. Keep stored-key mode and mark it long-lived.

## Out of scope
Operator host certificates (SM-6, done). Cloud and Kubernetes targets (WI-4).

## Deliver
Add a provider authentication mode `federated` per project and provider for Anthropic and OpenAI organisations with API billing. ## Out of scope
Gemini and Vertex AI. Subscription seat logins. The GitHub App.

## Acceptance
- With a fake provider token endpoint, an attempt in federated mode reaches the model API without any API key or OAuth token in its environment or files.

Source: docs/operations/workload-identitaet/index.html (AGT-3876), decisions WI-D1, WI-D2. ## Deliver
Let an enrolled host obtain an X.509-SVID (`spiffe://<td>/host/<host-id>`, URI SAN, at most 24 hours) by proving its current credential and a key pair generated on the host; the private key never leaves the host. # Runtime identity for hosted apps

Source: docs/operations/workload-identitaet/index.html (AGT-3876), decisions WI-D7, WI-D5.
